statusMeaning: ready means assignable; in-progress means implementation started; awaiting-verification means a tested implementation commit exists and independent verification is pending; no task is done without recorded technical verification and human acceptance

tasks.title: Create the canonical platform source tree
deliverables: Implement a deterministic assembler that materializes all 66 overlays in their actual dependency order, ending at DKC-036. Do not sort numerically. Handle the DKC-002 -> DKC-001 special case; reject cycles, missing dependencies and path escapes.
Commit the assembled source as platform/. Preserve 00-core/ and 01-step1/ as historical inputs. Future application changes go directly into platform/, not another chain of copied deliverables.

Record base commit, overlay order, per-file source and SHA256, and a pre-fix tree digest in platform provenance. Exclude caches, credentials and generated run output. Preserve license and attribution. Make the assembler safe on rerun: refuse an existing nonempty target by default.
Add a root validation entry point and update active documentation and an ADR for this migration. Carry contracts, package locks, tests and module manifests across without silently changing semantics.
Run the current focused and conformance suites, recording inherited failures accurately. This task establishes the tree; later assignments fix the security defects.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean Linux checkout materializes a byte-identical pre-fix platform tree twice without mutating source inputs. Provenance accounts for all 66 overlays and every canonical source file.
The assembler rejects an out-of-workspace target, a cycle, a missing predecessor and an attempted traversal; it cannot recursively overwrite user files.
Existing review probes can target platform/ and expose the known findings. Missing legacy evidence remains reported; no synthetic replacement logs.
All future task source paths resolve to platform/, and no changes are required in 00-core or historical deliverables.

tasks.title: Enforce server-owned protected-data classification
deliverables: Reproduce review R1 before changing behavior. Resolve data classification from trusted server registry state, never from action.protectedData. Derive the operation from the trusted tool/executor registration rather than action.operation.
Define how missing registry data and unavailable classification services fail closed for protected resources; distinguish an explicit ordinary classification from an unknown lookup.

Enforce no-AI-access, AI-read-only, append-only and retention-locked restrictions across reads, mutations, retrieval, logging and restore adapters. Caller metadata may only tighten policy, not lower it.
Add boundary regressions at runtime and relevant adapter entry points; retain valid ordinary-data workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: The paired R1 probe denies both baseline no-AI-access and caller-supplied ordinary/noAiAccess=false variants, with zero executor calls.
A mutating verb cannot be disguised as a read by action.operation; unknown or failed classification does not silently allow it.
Protected-data decisions preserve tenant scope and mandatory audit without copying forbidden data into logs; permitted ordinary reads still work.

tasks.title: Apply tenant and role authorization to every approval endpoint
deliverables: Reproduce R2 and R4. Authenticate list/read/view/create/decide/revoke/authorize routes, then apply operation-specific resource and tenant authorization consistently.

Filter list results by authorized tenant scope; require explicit tenant grants for cross-tenant platform actors. Treat missing tenant identity as denied unless a narrowly scoped platform grant applies.
Bind authorizeExecution access to the authenticated executor identity and server-owned request, instead of merely accepting any authenticated caller with a descriptor.

Prevent request-ID replacement and external mutation of approval state through returned object references. Apply the same checks to public service methods or explicitly separate trusted internal methods.
acceptanceCriteria: Anonymous approval listing returns 401/403 with no request IDs; tenant B cannot list, inspect, decide, revoke or consume tenant A requests.
The R2 probe returns 403, leaves the request pending and emits the permitted audit record. Explicit tenant-scoped platform access and legitimate human decisions still work.
Duplicate IDs, duplicate approvers, client-supplied identity/groups/training and client-supplied approved state fail safely.
HTTP and in-process tests cover both permitted and forbidden calls, including workload versus human actors.

tasks.title: Bind execution to the effective approval policy
deliverables: Reproduce R3 with two genuine approvals and a PDP decision requiring three. Carry the trusted policy decision into execution authorization and enforce the maximum of current PDP and approval-service requirements.

Bind approval verification to tenant, executor/agent identity as applicable, operation, target, parameters, artifact/plan/runbook digest, policy identity/version and expiry. Do not accept a caller-forged lower threshold or bundle version.
Validate thresholds as positive integers; enforce distinct eligible approvers, revocation and expiry at consumption. Preserve atomic one-time claims and restart behavior.
Add drift, replay, concurrency, unavailable-service and policy-change regressions; support genuinely preapproved standard changes only within the approved runbook scope.
acceptanceCriteria: R3 produces zero executions with two of three approvals; three valid approvers for the exact change allow one execution.
Increasing the required approval count or changing the trusted policy invalidates insufficient authorization; malformed thresholds fail closed.
Changed parameters/artifacts/tenant/target/actor and expired/revoked approvals do not execute; concurrent workers cannot double-consume an approval.
Valid bounded runbook execution and valid human-approved changes retain positive test coverage.

tasks.title: Create the integrated security acceptance command
deliverables: Expose one deterministic command that runs the R1-R4 regressions against the maintained platform entry points, alongside identity, role-separation, audit-failure and scope-boundary tests.
Keep positive controls and negative controls together. An unavailable audit/PDP/approval service must halt mutations; no agent may implement and approve its own work.
Emit a machine-readable report with tested commit, commands, exit codes, durations and evidence hashes. Distinguish local tests from live integrations.
Document unresolved integration gaps for Sprint 2; do not claim a full pentest, real HA or production readiness.
acceptanceCriteria: All four review security findings are closed with executable regressions and independently rerun evidence for the same source commit.
Tests use actual service boundaries where applicable, plus explicitly labeled stubs for external effects, and never customer data.
S1 exit package identifies remaining known packaging/platform failures instead of silently skipping them. Human acceptance is separate from this implementation report.

tasks.title: Make checkout integrity and path handling portable
deliverables: Fix R7 using platform-aware path containment. Reject absolute and parent traversal references and handle symlink escapes where evidence loading follows links.

Provide executable active shell entry points and consistent LF policy, with Windows-compatible developer commands where supported. Do not rewrite the archived overlay history just to make it look green.

Create a current artifact manifest containing only actually published source/evidence. Retain an explicit legacy-integrity report listing the 18 absent historical logs; never reconstruct them as original observations.
Scope generated artifacts and ignore rules so intended evidence is publishable, secret-bearing files are excluded and immutable audit requirements are preserved.
acceptanceCriteria: The prior Windows C-004 failure is fixed; intended Windows developer checks and the supported Linux checks pass.
A clean checkout can execute the active installer/validation scripts without manual chmod. The current artifact manifest verifies from a fresh clone.
Tampered or missing current files fail verification; historical missing logs are clearly separated from current release evidence.
Path traversal and relevant symlink escapes are rejected while valid module-relative references load.

tasks.title: Implement a real single-server installation profile
deliverables: Implement one supported Linux installation path, selecting an OS/runtime/deployment mechanism compatible with the actual code and recording the choice. Prefer the existing deployment approach when viable; do not introduce a second unmaintained orchestrator.

Build and wire the minimum real services: identity provider integration, policy, approval service, runtime with a harmless test executor, durable audit, persistent storage and basic health/telemetry. Surface missing service implementations as work to complete, not successful mocks.

Provide versioned configuration, validation and defaults for log level, retention, TLS/ingress, tenant identity, managed versus external database and separately configured external backup. Ordinary logging settings must not disable required audit.

Deliver preflight, install, status and diagnostics commands with meaningful exit codes, repeatable install behavior and persistent volumes. No embedded development keys or default production passwords; secrets are injected outside Git.
Document minimum measured CPU/RAM/disk and supported component versions. Mark the profile non-HA. Make a clean local disposable Linux VM usable before requiring a paid VPS.
acceptanceCriteria: A documented command installs and starts real processes from a clean supported Linux VM; replacing installer-live with another NOT RUN echo is not acceptance.
Authenticated API calls reach policy and approval services with durable audit. A reboot preserves tenant and approval data.
Invalid configuration fails before mutation; repeated installation does not destroy data. Missing secrets/TLS prerequisites cannot yield a healthy deployment.
The module dependency resolver selects only the minimal supported stack; unimplemented optional modules are not advertised as installed.

tasks.title: Run reproducible checks in GitHub CI
deliverables: Add root GitHub workflows for PRs and main covering clean checkout, current artifact integrity, schema checks, focused security regressions, conformance, build and a minimal service integration smoke test.
Pin third-party Actions to reviewed immutable commits and use least-privilege workflow permissions. PR validation must not receive deployment secrets or run untrusted code with elevated tokens.
Check DCO for newly introduced commits using an explicit trusted base; report historical unsigned commits separately without altering history or suppressing new violations.
Produce actual SBOM/scanner results where supported; unavailable scanners or required integrations cannot silently pass. Configure artifact retention and redaction.

Supply an idempotent branch-protection configuration/checker and exact required-check names. Apply repository settings only with repository-admin authorization; if access is missing, report that specific gate pending while finishing all code.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual GitHub PR run at the tested SHA completes the required jobs; local make output alone is not a GitHub CI result.
A negative fixture/security regression causes a failing required job, and unsigned newly introduced commits fail the DCO job.
Main requires passing checks and independent human review, or the report explicitly leaves admin activation pending. No automatic self-approval or bypass.
Workflow failure and missing jobs cannot be summarized as a passing release.

tasks.title: Prove readiness for VPS staging
deliverables: Automate a clean disposable Linux VM exercise: install, synthetic two-tenant login/API flow, service restart, full reboot, failure diagnostics and teardown limited to the test environment.
Bind evidence to exact commit/image digests and measured resource use. Derive a VPS sizing and storage specification from that evidence rather than inventing capacity.
Create a staging input template for host/SSH identity, domain/DNS, secret references, backup endpoint, allowed CIDRs, named human owner and budget cap; keep credentials out of Git.
Implement a readiness gate separating local functional success, GitHub CI, independent verification, human acceptance and missing infrastructure inputs.
acceptanceCriteria: The clean-VM run is reproduced independently with real services and persisted state; supported OS/runtime are explicit.
All S1 security gates and S2 installation/CI gates are met for the candidate commit. Missing admin settings remain a blocker, not a waiver.
The report gives a concrete server specification, backup requirements and operating cost inputs for the human to approve before any purchase.
S2 acceptance permits synthetic-data staging only; it does not assert HA, compliance certification or customer-production readiness.

tasks.title: Prepare and validate the authorized staging host
deliverables: Implement staging preflight/provisioning automation using the approved server specification and supplied connection details. If none are supplied, finish dry-runable code and report the required host/domain/backup inputs; do not purchase resources.
Limit deployment credentials to staging. Configure SSH access, explicit firewall/ingress rules, TLS and secret injection; preserve recovery access while changing networking.
Record host identity, OS/version, storage layout, component versions and the independent backup failure domain without exposing secrets.
Require an authorized executor identity for live host changes, separate from the implementer and verifier; bind the approved deployment to the candidate digest.
acceptanceCriteria: Read-only preflight confirms the intended host and backup destination; mismatched environment/host/digest or missing authorization stops deployment.
No customer data, main-branch mutation or production credentials are used. A VPS purchase is not triggered by running tests.
Recovery access and rollback for host configuration changes are verified before exposing services.

tasks.title: Deploy and verify the first real staging workflow
deliverables: Deploy the accepted candidate through the controlled staging deployment entry point. Record real endpoint and process/container health, image digests and TLS status.

Implement and execute a synthetic two-company workflow: login, create a harmless change request, collect the required distinct human approvals, execute a scoped action, inspect audit, revoke a test user and verify access loss.

Test unauthorized cross-tenant operations and the R1-R4 regressions through deployed API boundaries. Human approvals in the live exercise come from real participants; automated fixtures are labeled separate tests.
Feed performance/errors and unavailable collectors to the operations view; missing signals show unknown/stale, not healthy.
acceptanceCriteria: The workflow reaches real identity, approval, policy and audit components across process boundaries; results are linked by tenant/action/trace identifiers.
Two synthetic tenants remain isolated and revoked users cannot retain effective access beyond the documented token/session revocation behavior.
Service/PDP/audit failures produce controlled denial or halt, alerts and recoverable operator diagnostics. No unsupported self-healing privileges are added.

tasks.title: Prove persistence and independent backup recovery
deliverables: Run a consistent encrypted backup of synthetic platform state to the configured independent destination with separately scoped credentials.
Restore into an isolated replacement instance, validate records, tenant ACLs, approval state and audit continuity, then test retention/holds and credential recovery.

Measure backup age, acknowledged records recovered, recovery time and any actual loss against the declared profile RPO/RTO. Exercise restart and storage errors without destroying the only viable backup.
Preserve protected-data restrictions and deletion/hold semantics during restore. Record any unsupported WORM enforcement rather than representing a local flag as immutable storage.
acceptanceCriteria: Recovery succeeds without reading the original instance data volumes; the backup is not merely another directory on the same server.
Recovered data and authorization are validated per tenant; logs contain no secrets or forbidden payloads.
Measured results meet the approved staging profile objectives or the gate fails with actual measurements. An unexecuted drill is NOT RUN.

tasks.title: Prove upgrade rollback and human takeover
deliverables: Execute a controlled upgrade and deliberate failed-release scenario using synthetic state. Validate migration compatibility, rollback to the prior accepted artifact and data integrity.
Exercise agent kill switch, credential revocation, escalation and human takeover through a bounded, preapproved recovery runbook. No unrestricted shell/root or self-approval.
Produce the staging acceptance report with linked deployment, workflow, backup/recovery and rollback evidence for the exact artifacts.

List the next HA/multi-server verification work explicitly: quorum, split brain, partitions, failover, fencing, worker coordination and independent failure domains. These are subsequent work, not claims made by this single-server sprint.
acceptanceCriteria: Upgrade and rollback preserve data and permissions; an irreversible migration cannot advertise automatic rollback without a tested recovery alternative.
An authorized human can halt agents and take over; unauthorized actors cannot disable audit or mutate protected data.
Independent verifier and human owner accept the measured single-server staging evidence. Production/HA readiness remains false until separate live gates are fulfilled.
